messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — api-gateway (eu-west) elevated 5xx rate detected :rotating_light:

incident-bot: metric: gateway.5xx_rate = 7.9% (5m avg), baseline 0.3% — paging oncall

jon (oncall): taking this. starting triage. assigning sprints: gateway, edge, infra.

maya: on logs now, pulling recent proxy traces. seeing a lot of upstream timeouts + 502 from mux layer.

ops-anna: customers? any traffic skew to large clients?

jon (oncall): customer-impact: brief spike across many routes, some clients seeing failures on /v1/generate and /batch. Not yet widespread but increasing error counts.

kevin: checking rollout history — no recent gateway deploys in last 3h.

maya: reproducing a sample request that fails:

```
POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Content-Type: application/json
{ "model": "rwd-13b", "prompt": "hi" }
```

maya: gateway logs show: `upstream response: 502 Bad Gateway` and repeated `dial tcp ... i/o timeout` to inference-proxy pool.

jon (oncall): sounds like upstream capacity or transient network. can infra confirm host health & SG rules?

ops-anna: edge and infra health checks look ok for nodes. but one autoscale group shows recent AZ imbalance, several instances entering `draining` around 13:04.

kevin: routing telemetry: increased retries from edge to gateway causing connection pool pressure. qps to a subset of gateway pods jumped 4x due to a burst of long-running streaming sessions.

maya: quick mitigation idea: enable circuit-breaker on high-latency routes and reduce keepalive to free connections. also enable short-lived fallback to smaller model instance to reduce backend latency.

jon (oncall): agree. will flip circuit-breaker to 1m timeout for /v1/generate and enable routing to standby region for critical customers. triggering change now.

deploy-bot: rollout started: ops/circuit-breaker-502-mitigation v1 -> 7 pods updated (canary 1 pod)

kevin: watchpool: temporarily increase connection pool size on gateway-proxy to avoid immediate rejections? could help while breakers stabilize.

ops-anna: making connection pool sizing change (hot patch) on 3 gateway nodes.

maya: continuing to sample traces — KV cache hit rate dropped at the same time as spike. suspect KV cache eviction/invalidation + heavy streaming increased backend load.

jon (oncall): customer comms: outreach to top 3 affected customers via CSMs. noting degraded generation success rate and ongoing mitigation.

sara: filing post-incident ticket for cache eviction root cause + demand surge testing.

deploy-bot: rollout status: canary healthy for 90s, no immediate increase in error rate for canary. continuing staged rollout.

jon (oncall): error rate dropping to 2.1% (5m). continuing to monitor for 30m. leaving command post active for handoff in 20m.

ops-anna: connection pool patch applied, rolling restart avoided. AZ balance restoring as drained instances finish decommission.

maya: saved trace snippets for postmortem:

```
[TRACE] gateway->inference-proxy x-request-id=abc123 latency=1.2s status=502 upstream_err=dial_timeout
[TRACE] kv-cache miss=0.78 seq_len_median=512
```

jon (oncall): thanks team. I'll hand off to next oncall in 20m. if anything spikes, re-open this thread and ping @oncall.

kevin: recommend follow-ups: synthetic load test for streaming sessions, connection pool autoscaling, and tighter routing circuit-breaker defaults.

sara: noted. creating follow-up tickets and tagging eng-runtime, eng-ml for model-side tuning.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — status: mitigated (error rate reduced). incident channel will remain open for 30m for observation.

jon (oncall): handoff in 20m to @kevin (next-oncall). leaving notes in pager duty. good recovery so far :thumbsup:
